title: Quantile-cohort batcher with cache-aware routing and kernel-placement optimizations
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: reduce padding waste and improve KV cache hit-rate for mixed-length traffic while placing work on kernels that minimize per-token compute cost. This PR introduces a quantile-driven cohorter that groups arriving requests into fine-grained quantile cohorts at enqueue time, then uses a cache-aware routing policy plus kernel-cost heuristics to form execution batches. The design targets continuous-batching use cases (low-latency steady traffic) and bursty traffic by dynamically switching cohort merge policies. Key features: 1) Quantile cohorting: compute approximate length quantiles on a sliding window and assign arriving requests to the nearest cohort to limit intra-batch padding; 2) Cache-priority routing: prefer forming batches that maximize KV cache reuse (prefix-sharing coalescing) by scoring candidates based on recent cache footprint; 3) Kernel-placement heuristic: consult a lightweight kernel-cost table (per architecture + sequence-length-range) to prefer GPU kernels and lane alignment that reduce overall token compute; 4) Dual-mode batching: continuous mode (aggressive low-latency cohorts) and opportunistic-mode (maximize throughput under high queue occupancy); 5) Safety fallbacks: when cohorts are sparse, fall back to length-tolerant packing with bounded padding budget; 6) Telemetry + evals: new metrics (cohort_size_hist, cohort_padding_bytes, cohort_kv_hit_rate, kernel_choice_distribution) and a small perf harness to drive realistic mixed-length workloads. Implementation: changes are localized to runtime/batcher and runtime/scheduler with a small public API addition to allow tuning cohort quantile window and padding budget per route. No changes to public REST API. Benchmark summary: on mixed-length TTFB-sensitive workload (40% short <=16 tokens, 50% medium 17-128 tokens, 10% long >512 tokens) we see median latency unchanged, p95 latency improved by ~8% due to reduced padding overhead, token throughput per GPU improved +6% at 95th percentile, and estimated token cost reduced by ~5% for the workload profile. KV cache hit-rate improved from 22% to 37% in the same runs due to prioritized prefix coalescing. Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated pools with canary traffic first, monitor new metrics and rollback if cohort_padding_bytes or p95 latency regress by more than configured thresholds. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-9821) - [x] unit tests for cohort assignment and scoring - [x] integration tests with scheduler and kernel stub - [x] perf harness and benchmark reproducer - [x] added telemetry and dashboards - [x] documented public tuning knobs

release_notes: Introduce quantile-driven cohort batching with cache-aware routing and kernel-placement heuristics to reduce padding waste and improve KV cache reuse. New tuning knobs: cohort.quantile_window, cohort.padding_budget, cohort.kv_smoothing_alpha. Telemetry: cohort_padding_bytes, cohort_kv_hit_rate, kernel_choice_distribution.
